/-!
# Erdős Problem 646

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/646](https://www.erdosproblems.com/646)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
- [Be97] Berend, Daniel, *On the parity of exponents in the factorization of $n!$*.
  J. Number Theory (1997), 13-19.
-/

open scoped Nat

namespace Erdos646

/--
Let $p_1,\ldots,p_k$ be distinct primes. Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $n!$ is
divisible by an even power of each of the $p_i$?

The answer is yes, proved by Berend [Be97], who further proved that the sequence of such $n$
has bounded gaps (where the bound depends on the initial set of primes).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos646.lean"]
theorem erdos_646 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime) →
      {n : ℕ | ∀ p ∈ S, Even (padicValNat p (n !))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos646

reformulations.difference: The finite family of distinct primes is represented by a Finset; the empty family and the inputs n = 0, 1 are allowed.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Taking the image of an injective tuple gives the corresponding Finset, and Finset.equivFin enumerates any Finset without repetitions. The valuation predicates agree under these conversions; their universally quantified infinitude statements were proved equivalent in scratch. The empty family gives all natural numbers. Removing n = 0, 1, or any finite initial segment does not change infinitude, also proved in scratch.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the source’s question. Erdős–Graham p. 77 explicitly concerns even exponents in the prime decomposition, confirming that exact p-adic valuation—not merely divisibility by some square—is intended. Proved the exact-divisibility characterization in Lean and tested small factorials and prime sets. Primality excludes exceptional bases, and factorials never reach padicValNat’s zero-input default. The source’s stronger bounded-gap result is background, so its absence from the theorem is not a defect. The cited external proof was kernel-checked in a scratch copy after three tactic-only compatibility changes for the newer local Lean/Mathlib; a bridge proves the repository’s exact proposition using only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The full texts of Er97e and Be97 could not be retrieved; their available bibliographic records/review were consulted, while the exact statement was verified against the source’s LaTeX page and ErGr80. All experiments are under /workspace/review, and the target file remains identical to the committed version.
